key_insight: CPA-NAMD-extF extends classical-path nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to simulate field-driven electronic responses, revealing fluctuation-sensitive opto-currents in a 2D hybrid perovskite.
engineering_relevance: The method could help researchers study how finite-temperature structural motion affects optoelectronic responses in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Propagate a first-principles electronic density matrix along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
Include explicit external-field coupling and self-consistent electronic-density updates.
Apply the framework to SiO₂ optical absorption and (BA)₂CsPb₂Br₇ opto-currents.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks show close agreement with regular TDDFT for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses; perovskite calculations reveal Br-centered vortex currents.
watch_item: Precomputed classical ionic trajectories do not capture field-induced changes to ionic motion, so applicability requires care when that feedback is important.
paper_title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
